paths.description: Public marketing entry page and app acquisition journey; tests first impression, preferences, responsive layout and global metadata.
Primary browse/search landing page; represents discovery navigation and the search entry point.
Wallpaper category/listing template; represents media grids, advertising, filtering, search and repeated scrolling.
Search journey from the category header to a results route for “cats”.
Wallpaper detail/download template; represents the core content-to-download journey and structured product-like metadata.
Unknown route used to inspect HTTP/navigation recovery messaging.

findings.summary: The site forces its dark palette even when the system requests light mode.
findings.evidence: The default and prefers-color-scheme: light screenshots are pixel-identical (both 284,440 bytes) and remain #141414/dark; the root is authored with class="dark".
findings.suggestedFix: Let the user/system select theme: declare color-scheme: light dark and drive tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), while preserving a manual override.

findings.summary: Route changes do not expose authored View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The category-to-/find/cats search navigation completed, but inspected page CSS contained no authored view-transition-name treatment for the route/content swap.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document or same-document View Transitions for search and detail navigation, with reduced-motion-safe fallbacks.

findings.summary: The sticky navigation remains static instead of reflecting scroll state.
findings.evidence: Desktop and long mobile captures show a fixed-height sticky header with no progress or scrolled-state treatment across pages up to 8,802px tall.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state container query or lightweight declarative progress treatment so long listings communicate position without JS scroll handlers.

findings.summary: Dropdown/overlay positioning is implemented as custom component chrome rather than anchored positioning.
findings.evidence: The category probe found a Radix-style aria-haspopup="dialog" category control and custom BaseDropdown CSS, with no position-anchor/position-try use in the inspected component.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for the category menu so it remains attached and viewport-safe.

findings.summary: The consent experience can cover almost the entire mobile viewport on entry.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a modal consent notice from y=72 to y=751 in a 823px-tall mobile viewport, with copy referring to 1,078 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the full-height first-load consent wall with a compact, equally actionable notice; defer non-essential partners until an affirmative choice.

findings.summary: Major overlays are custom div-based modal components instead of native dialog/popover primitives.
findings.evidence: Inspected CSS defines fixed .Modal_modal and overlay divs; the consent UI is a div role=dialog rather than a native dialog, increasing custom focus/dismiss complexity.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for modal flows and popover for transient menus, with native Escape/light-dismiss behavior and explicit focus return.

findings.summary: Advertising and two-tier navigation consume a disproportionate share of content views.
findings.evidence: The category first viewport allocates a 300x250 block to an “AD” beside only two content cards, and browse adds two stacked navigation rows before content.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve smaller, deferred ad slots below the first content row and simplify duplicated category chrome on narrow/initial views.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly rendered on the primary search field.
findings.evidence: After programmatically focusing #search, activeElement was correct but the focus container computed outline was “none 3px” and box-shadow “none”.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring to the search container/button and verify keyboard focus across icon-only controls.

findings.summary: Cold mobile loading misses the good LCP range by a wide margin.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 5.6s, LCP 8.8s, Speed Index 12.4s and performance 56; the independent trace measured LCP 3.34s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the hero/LCP image, reduce critical CSS/third parties, and verify LCP below 2.5s under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: The homepage ships a 4.8MB, 99-request critical load dominated by oversized decorative images.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 4,814,216 transferred bytes: 3,486,822 image bytes and 1,212,183 script bytes. A single ctype_bg PNG was 2,127,404 bytes; Lighthouse estimated 2.1MB image savings and 2.2s render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Convert and responsively size decorative PNGs, preload only the LCP candidate, defer offscreen assets, and shorten cache/render-blocking chains.

findings.summary: Large script payloads and unused client code are shipped before users need them.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 65 scripts / 1.21MB; Lighthouse estimated 163KiB unused JavaScript and 14KiB unused CSS, plus 11KiB legacy JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Split route code, conditionally load advertising/analytics after consent and interaction, and remove duplicated/legacy bundles.

findings.summary: Many important icon/image links have no accessible name.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse link-name failed for the logo, three app-download links, footer logo, five social links and repeated footer app links; its agent tree also flagged role=heading on an img.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon-only link a concise accessible name, use semantic headings instead of role=heading on images, and keep decorative images alt="".

findings.summary: Consent links fail WCAG AA contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured #7c54eb on #1c1c1c at 3.5:1 for 12px consent links; 4.5:1 is required.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise the consent-link foreground contrast to at least 4.5:1 in all themes and states.

findings.summary: The keyboard/accessibility structure breaks on unnamed links and invisible search focus.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found multiple tabbable links without discernible text; the active search control had no visible outline or shadow in the focus probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Name all interactive elements, use semantic landmarks/headings, and implement an obvious consistent :focus-visible treatment.

findings.summary: Several logo images lack intrinsic dimensions and responsive delivery.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 4 missing-dimension images, 4 oversized images, 4 missing srcset and 4 legacy PNG/JPG assets; Lighthouse unsized-images identified header/footer logos.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio and serve responsive modern-format logo/decorative assets.

findings.summary: The document is excluded from the back/forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported CacheControlNoStoreCookieModified: cache-control:no-store prevents BFCache restoration.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid no-store on public pages that do not contain sensitive data and make cookie updates BFCache-compatible.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used, but CSP/HSTS are absent and one long-lived cookie is not Secure.
findings.evidence: Headers primitive found no Content-Security-Policy or Strict-Transport-Security. Cookies found didomi_dcs Secure=false with a 366-day expiry; two first-party cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash CSP, HSTS after subdomain review, and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest viable SameSite/lifetime.

findings.summary: A large advertising/analytics surface is active on the public landing page.
findings.evidence: Tracker audit found 15 third-party origins and Google trackers; HAR measured 29 third-party requests / 903,267 bytes, while consent copy names 1,078 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to essential-only requests, cut partner count, batch first-party analytics, and load ad/analytics code only after meaningful consent.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defense headers are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS or Permissions-Policy; X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, nosniff and Referrer-Policy were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP frame-ancestors/script-src, HSTS and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; consider Trusted Types for the large client application.

findings.summary: The app-like site advertises installability but no active offline controller was observed.
findings.evidence: A valid standalone web app manifest exists, but the platform probe found no service-worker controller during the audited session.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a service worker and provide an explicit offline shell/fallback for browsed and previously viewed content, or stop presenting the site as standalone-installable.

findings.summary: Visible dates use a fixed English ordering rather than clearly locale-aware formatting.
findings.evidence: The detail template renders “2024 Aug 5” while html lang is en; the site has multilingual category content but no locale-adapted date was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Format dates/numbers through Intl.DateTimeFormat/Intl.NumberFormat using the active locale.

findings.summary: Decorative image delivery is far heavier than the experience requires.
findings.evidence: Images account for 3.49MB; two background PNGs total 2.99MB, and Lighthouse estimates 2.1MB could be saved through image delivery improvements.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants at displayed sizes and use responsive image-set/srcset for decorative and content imagery.

findings.summary: Background advertising and analytics code adds substantial work before user intent.
findings.evidence: The first load executes 65 scripts and contacts 15 third-party origins; ad, prebid, consent, dual Google Analytics and Cloudflare scripts appear in the inspected script list.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load non-essential dependencies after consent/interaction, consolidate analytics, and deprioritise background fetches.

findings.summary: Third-party and decorative-media bytes are disproportionate on a simple marketing entry page.
findings.evidence: The load transfers 4.81MB, including 903KB third-party and nearly 3MB in two decorative backgrounds, before any core browse action.
findings.suggestedFix: Set explicit page/third-party budgets, defer ad stacks, and replace oversized decorative raster backgrounds with lighter responsive assets.

taskList.title: Cut the image, script and third-party critical load
Restore accessible names, focus visibility and contrast
Add CSP, HSTS, Permissions-Policy and tighten cookies
Replace intrusive/custom overlays with compact native primitives
Respect system theme and improve navigational motion/state
Fix intrinsic image sizing and BFCache eligibility
Add an offline fallback for the installable experience
